title: Converting fractions, decimals and percentages

match.reason: The bank point covers the same three-way conversion but is broader, adding a number line section on negative fractions and a question on it that goes beyond the brief, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Converting fractions, decimals and percentages
card: A percentage is a fraction out of 100. The symbol % means \(\frac{1}{100}\), so \(7\% = \frac{7}{100} = 0.07\).
To change a percentage to a decimal, divide by 100. To change a decimal to a percentage, multiply by 100.
To change a fraction to a decimal, divide the top by the bottom. Then multiply by 100 for a percentage.
draft.remember: Divide by 100 to go from a percentage to a decimal. Multiply by 100 to go back.

a.q: Which decimal is the same as \(45\%\)?
a.why: Divide by 100 to change a percentage to a decimal, so \(45 \div 100 = 0.45\). Choosing \(4.5\) comes from dividing by 10 instead of 100.

b.q: Mia scored \(\frac{7}{20}\) on a quiz. What is her score as a percentage?
b.why: Divide to get \(7 \div 20 = 0.35\), then multiply by 100 to get \(35\%\). The answer \(0.35\%\) is tempting, but it leaves out the step of multiplying by 100.
b.clue: Divide the top by the bottom first, then multiply by 100.
